Jaspar Carmichael-Jack 11 minutes read · Jul 25, 2026 Key Takeaways AiSDR is a strong tool: transparent published pricing ($250 to $2,500 a month per its site), fast setup, and both outbound and inbound coverage. Teams usually leave it when they outgrow it, not when it fails: enterprise governance, central ops, and deep CRM controls are thinner than a large org needs. The strongest alternative is an AI BDR that owns the whole motion and carries enterprise weight, not just another SMB agent. Artisan runs on usage-based credits with no platform fee, so a large team's cost stays flat instead of climbing per seat. Over 90% of Artisan customers run Ava autonomously, and CookUnity generated pipeline at roughly $45 per lead across over 100,000 emails. Match the pick to your stage and stack; this page routes you by both. The best AiSDR alternative is Artisan, whose AI business development representative (BDR), Ava, owns the full outbound job with the enterprise governance and CRM depth that small and medium-sized business (SMB) tools lack: central-ops deployment, a control dial, and a full audit trail. Amplemarket, Regie.ai, Reply.io, and Salesforce Agentforce are the other real options. This page ranks them and says who each is wrong for. What AiSDR does well, and where teams outgrow it Give AiSDR its due first. It solved the two things buyers hate most about this category: opaque pricing and slow setup. Its tiers are published ($250, $900, and $2,500 a month per its site), you can be up and running fast, it handles outbound and inbound, and its "Ami" strategist agent guides the motion. For an SMB or lower mid-market team, that transparency and speed are a real reason to buy, and plenty of teams are happy on it. For a fuller breakdown, see AiSDR pricing and reviews . The reason to look elsewhere is rarely a defect; it is growth.
